business: CollegeStat (collegestat.xyz): online help for Central Asian families whose child applies for a bachelor's abroad
by_segment: Affluent parent aiming for US/UK top universities
Upper-middle parent aiming for UK/Europe/Canada with partial scholarship
Middle-income parent aiming for low-tuition Europe/Asia (Germany, Korea, Turkey, Poland)
Student doing it alone, parents support but don't manage it
by_behaviour: Ambitious, will pay for top results
why_not: I have never heard of CollegeStat in any of our Telegram channels, and I don't pay a foreign card to a company nobody in my group chat can vouch for. For a US/UK top-university application I would rather pay a known consultant properly; $99 for 'unlimited essay review' sounds too good to be serious.

I don't know who you are, and paying a website I just met by card with promises of refunds is exactly how my friend lost money to an agency. The local agencies and my child's IELTS centre already help us for free, so I'd use your free search and maybe the one practice application, but not pay.

I don't have time to run applications myself, and this still sounds like my child and I have to do the work, just with a checklist. On top of that it wants an international card, which I almost never use, so I would try the free part and stop there.

For Harvard or Oxford I want a person who runs the whole thing and calls me, not a website my child has to drive alone. At $99 it looks like a software tool, not a service that takes this off my plate.

$99 is about two weeks of my family's income, and we already pay for IELTS prep. For Germany, Poland or Turkey I can check deadlines and costs on the university sites myself, so I will use the free part and maybe the free practice uni-assist application, and stop there.

$99 is almost a week and a half of what I earn, paid by an international card I barely use, and for Germany or Poland the university sites and ChatGPT already tell me most deadlines for free. I would use the free part, the search and one practice uni-assist application, and see if that is enough.

I want someone who raises my child's chances at the best schools, and this sells checked deadlines and a plan, which I could get from the Telegram channels I already read. It doesn't guarantee admission, so what are we paying for? I'd try the free practice application, but I would not pay yet.

We are aiming at top UK and Canadian universities with a scholarship, and this sounds like a deadline checklist, not someone who gets my child into Oxford or UofT. For paperwork the local agency already helps for free, and for real strategy I would pay a proper consultant, not $99 online.

We already pay for IELTS prep, and my son is building his shortlist with ChatGPT, EducationUSA and the universities' own websites. I'd use the free search and the one practice application, but I don't see a reason to pay yet when all the deadline and cost information is public anyway.

We're looking at UK, Europe and Canada, and my son is already making a list with ChatGPT and the university websites, which cost nothing. $99 by international card for something we can mostly do ourselves is hard for me to justify. I'd use the free search and the one practice application and stop there.
